name: विश्वरूपदर्शनयोग
meaning: The Vision of the Cosmic Form
teaching: Arjuna asks to see — and is given eyes no mortal has. The universal form is not a comfort: it is all faces, all fires, all futures, armies streaming into blazing mouths, time itself declaring 'I am become Death, destroyer of worlds.' Arjuna, terrified, begs for the familiar face back. Some truth can be witnessed only briefly; love restores the human scale in which we can live. Theology becomes sight: the universal form blazes, devours, and overwhelms — and then mercy restores the gentle face. The vision's price is undivided love; its final lesson, friendship to every being.
questions: Arjuna learns the warriors are 'already slain' — he is only the instrument. Where might you be an instrument of something already in motion?
What truth have you glimpsed that was too large to hold — and what did you do with it?
Why do you think the vision ends with a request for the gentle, familiar form?

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.devanagari:
मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम् ।
यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम॥
verses.transliteration:
madanugrahāya paramaṃ guhyamadhyātmasaṃjñitam
yattvayoktaṃ vacastena moho'yaṃ vigato mama
verses.essence: Arjuna says: by your grace toward me, the supreme secret of the Self has been spoken — and my delusion is gone.
verses.translation: By this word (explanation) of the highest secret concerning the Self which Thou hast spoken, for the sake of blessing me, my delusion is gone.

anvaya.form: compound noun, masculine, dative singular (for the sake of)
anvaya.parts: मत् (me) + अनुग्रह (favour): favour toward me

anvaya.form: adjective, neuter, nominative singular (describing the word)

anvaya.base: गुह्य · to be hidden, secret (√गुह् · to hide)

anvaya.meaning: called the teaching on the Self
anvaya.base: अध्यात्म · concerning the Self; संज्ञित · named
anvaya.parts: अध्यात्म (concerning the Self) + संज्ञित (named): bearing the name 'concerning the Self'

verses.explanation: Arjuna opens with gratitude and a claim he believes: moho 'yaṁ vigataḥ — the confusion is gone. He has heard ten chapters of doctrine and understood them. What this chapter will teach him is the distance between understanding a thing and seeing it.
verses.connection: Receipt for the teaching on the Self (chapters 2–6, as Rāmānuja and Śrīdhara read it) — the prelude to asking for more than words.
verses.reflection: Notice the gap in yourself between understanding a truth and having seen it — honor both stages.
verses.background: Arjuna, his delusion dissolved by the words just heard, makes the boldest request in scripture: You have spoken the supreme mystery and I have heard Your glories — now, if You think me able to bear it, O Lord of yoga, show me Your imperishable cosmic Self with my own eyes.
verses.hook: What happened to Arjuna's confusion after hearing Krishna's teaching?

views.text: Arjuna's delusion, his non-discriminating idea, is removed by the supremely secret teaching on the Self, which discriminates between the Self and the non-Self, given out of favour to him.
The delusion that is lifted is the mistaking of the body for the self; the 'secret about the Self' is the teaching running from 2.12 to 6.46.
Arjuna now wants to perceive with his own eye what the last chapter taught; a truth learned from instruction becomes fully clear only when grasped by direct perception.
The delusion named here is the thought 'I am the killer, these are killed', removed because the teaching showed that the Self is not the doer.
Arjuna now accepts Krishna not only as his friend but as the Supreme Person, the source of all glory, and gratefully acknowledges the compassion behind this teaching.

verses.devanagari:
भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया ।
त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम्॥
verses.transliteration:
bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṃ śrutau vistaraśo mayā
tvattaḥ kamalapatrākṣa māhātmyamapi cāvyayam
verses.essence: The origin and dissolution of beings I have heard from you in detail — and also your imperishable greatness.
verses.translation: The origin and the destruction of beings verily have been heard by me in detail from Thee, O lotus-eyed Lord, and also Thy inexhaustible greatness.

anvaya.base: भव · coming into being; अप्यय · passing away
anvaya.form: compound noun, masculine, nominative dual (the pair, subject)
anvaya.parts: भव (origin) + अप्यय (dissolution): origin and dissolution together

anvaya.form: past participle, masculine, nominative dual (the two, heard)

anvaya.base: कमल · lotus; पत्र · leaf, petal; अक्षि · eye
anvaya.parts: कमल (lotus) + पत्र (leaf) + अक्ष (eye): one whose eyes are like lotus leaves

verses.explanation: The inventory of what he holds: cosmology, the births and ends of all beings, the catalogue of glories — all śrutau, *heard*. Note the address, kamala-patrākṣa, lotus-eyed: even while preparing to ask for the cosmic, he is looking at the gentle human face he knows.
verses.connection: Summarizes the vibhuti teaching of ch10 — heard, detailed, and not yet enough.
verses.reflection: Inventory what you have heard but not yet beheld — let the list become a prayer, not a complaint.
verses.background: Arjuna, his delusion dissolved by the words just heard, makes the boldest request in scripture: You have spoken the supreme mystery and I have heard Your glories — now, if You think me able to bear it, O Lord of yoga, show me Your imperishable cosmic Self with my own eyes.
verses.hook: What has Arjuna learned so far about where beings come from and go?

views.text: Arjuna has heard from Krishna in detail, not briefly, the origin and dissolution of beings, and also his undecaying glory.
What was heard in chapters 7–10 is that all other beings arise from and dissolve into Him, and His rule over everything; the particle hi signals the longing for the vision about to be revealed.

His 'imperishable greatness' is that, though He creates the world and dispenses the fruits of action, He stays unchanged, impartial and unattached; seeing beings as dependent on Him removes the notion 'I am the doer'.
Kamala-patra can also mean knowledge of the Self, so 'lotus-eyed' hints at the One who is reached through that knowledge.
Arjuna confirms Krishna as the source of creation and dissolution, present in all yet untouched by their flaws, impartial dispenser of karma, and so worthy of everyone's adoration.

verses.devanagari:
एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर ।
द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम॥
verses.transliteration:
evametadyathāttha tvamātmānaṃ parameśvara
draṣṭumicchāmi te rūpamaiśvaraṃ puruṣottama
verses.essence: As you declare yourself, O supreme Lord, so it is. Yet I desire to see your lordly form, Purushottama.
verses.translation: (Now) O Supreme Lord, as Thou hast thus described Thyself, O Supreme Person, I wish to see Thy divine form.

anvaya.form: verb, perfect form with present sense, 2nd person singular

anvaya.parts: परम (supreme) + ईश्वर (lord): the supreme Lord

anvaya.base: ऐश्वर · belonging to the Lord (from ईश्वर)

anvaya.parts: पुरुष (person) + उत्तम (highest): the highest Person

verses.explanation: The pivot of the whole Gita's middle: evam etat — I believe every word — *and* draṣṭum icchāmi, I want to see. Not doubt asking for proof, but love asking for presence; faith that has matured to the point of wanting its object unveiled. The boldest request a creature has made.
verses.connection: Converts ch10's heard glories into the demand for direct vision.
verses.reflection: Let your faith mature into Arjuna's boldness once: I believe You — and I long to see.
verses.background: Arjuna, his delusion dissolved by the words just heard, makes the boldest request in scripture: You have spoken the supreme mystery and I have heard Your glories — now, if You think me able to bear it, O Lord of yoga, show me Your imperishable cosmic Self with my own eyes.
verses.hook: Why would Arjuna, already convinced, still ask to see Krishna's form?

views.text: 'So it is, not otherwise' — yet he still wishes to see the form of Viṣṇu endowed with knowledge, sovereignty, power, strength, valour and splendour.
Arjuna wants to realise directly the form proper to the Lord alone: sovereign, protector, creator, destroyer and support of all, distinct from every other entity.
Arjuna stresses he has no disbelief at all; he asks to see the lordly form out of eager wonder.
If tiny souls have a personality, God has the supreme one, along with an impersonal aspect. Arjuna fully accepts Krishna's personal form yet longs to see the universal form with his own eyes.

verses.devanagari:
मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो ।
योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयात्मानमव्ययम्॥
verses.transliteration:
manyase yadi tacchakyaṃ mayā draṣṭumiti prabho
yogeśvara tato me tvaṃ darśayātmānamavyayam
verses.essence: If you think it can be seen by me, O Lord — then, master of yoga, show me your imperishable Self.
verses.translation: If Thou, O Lord, thinkest it possible for me to see it, do Thou, then, O Lord of the Yogins, show me Thy imperishable Self.

anvaya.form: gerundive used as adjective, neuter, nominative singular

anvaya.base: thus — marks a thought or quote

anvaya.parts: योग (yoga, or yogis) + ईश्वर (lord): lord of yoga

verses.explanation: The request, perfectly mannered: yadi manyase — if *you* judge me able. Arjuna does not presume capacity; he submits his eyes for assessment. And he names the right office: yogeśvara, Lord of yoga — for what he asks requires not just willingness to show but power to make showable.
verses.connection: Completes 11.3's plea with the humility that makes granting it possible.
verses.reflection: Ask for the great things conditionally, as he did: if You judge me able — then show me.
verses.background: Arjuna, his delusion dissolved by the words just heard, makes the boldest request in scripture: You have spoken the supreme mystery and I have heard Your glories — now, if You think me able to bear it, O Lord of yoga, show me Your imperishable cosmic Self with my own eyes.
verses.hook: How does Arjuna ask to see the universal form?

views.text: 'Lord of Yoga' means Lord of yogis, since Yoga here stands for yogis. Very eager, Arjuna asks to be shown the Lord's eternal Self, if Krishna thinks it possible for him to see it.
Avyayam is read as an adverb, 'completely': reveal everything about Yourself. 'Yoga' in Yogeśvara means His auspicious attributes, as 11.8 will call it 'My lordly yoga'.
Merely wishing to see is no ground for being shown, so Arjuna adds the condition: only if You judge that I am able.
This vision can be had only through His grace; the Lord of yoga is the one who can bestow on a fit seeker the realisation of identity with the Absolute.
Arjuna humbly seeks permission, asking Krishna to reveal it only if he finds him worthy, and his new address, Lord of all yogis, shows his growing reverence.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.devanagari:
पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ।
नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च॥
verses.transliteration:
paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ
nānāvidhāni divyāni nānāvarṇākṛtīni ca
verses.essence: The Blessed Lord says: behold my forms, Partha — by hundreds and by thousands, divine, of many kinds, many colors and shapes.
verses.translation: Behold, O Arjuna, forms of Mine, by the hundreds and thousands, of different sorts, divine, and of various colours and shapes.

anvaya.parts: नाना (various) + विधा (kind): of various kinds
नाना (various) + वर्ण (colour) + आकृति (shape): having various colours and shapes

verses.explanation: Consent, and immediately the grammar strains: paśya, see — but rūpāṇi, *forms*, plural by hundreds and thousands. Arjuna asked to see one supreme form; he is told the supreme form is a multitude. The first lesson of the vision arrives before the vision: the One does not come in ones.
verses.connection: The granting of 11.4 — with a plural that already exceeds the request.
verses.reflection: Prepare to be exceeded: ask the One for one thing and expect hundreds in answer.
verses.background: Krishna consents and exceeds the asking: behold My forms by the hundreds and thousands, all the gods and wonders never seen before, the whole universe standing as one in My body — but you cannot see Me with these eyes of yours; I give you the divine eye. Behold My sovereign yoga.
verses.hook: What does Krishna first tell Arjuna to look at?

views.text: The forms are countless, in hundreds and thousands, celestial and supernatural, with different colours such as blue and yellow, and with their parts arranged in different shapes.
These forms are the foundation of all things — supernatural, multicoloured and varied in configuration.
The form is one; 'forms' is plural only because it is so manifold. Before showing it, Krishna first rouses Arjuna to full attention.
Every grade of being is there — fat and lean, rich and poor, waking and sleeping — with all the colours of sky, silk, twilight, coal, snow and leaf.
Krishna bids Arjuna to pay attention: the universal form is one, yet holds innumerable divine figures of countless shapes and colours.

verses.devanagari:
पश्यादित्यान्वसून्रुद्रानश्विनौ मरुतस्तथा ।
बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याश्चर्याणि भारत॥
verses.transliteration:
paśyādityānvasūnrudrānaśvinau marutastathā
bahūnyadṛṣṭapūrvāṇi paśyāścaryāṇi bhārata
verses.essence: Behold the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Ashvins, the Maruts. Behold many wonders never seen before, Bharata.
verses.translation: Behold the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Asvins and also the Maruts; behold many wonders never seen before, O Arjuna.

anvaya.base: आदित्य · son of Aditi, a sun-god
वसु · a class of eight gods
रुद्र · storm-god, a class of eleven
अश्विन् · the twin horsemen, physicians of the gods

anvaya.parts: अदृष्ट (not seen) + पूर्व (before): not seen before

verses.explanation: The guest list: every order of divinity Vedic ears had only chanted about — sun-gods, storm-hosts, the healers of heaven — now gathered into one viewing. Adṛṣṭa-pūrvāṇi, never before seen: the phrase will return at 11.45, in Arjuna's mixed delight and fear; he is being shown what no eye has held.
verses.connection: Itemizes 11.5's thousands: the whole pantheon, in one body.
verses.reflection: Expect wonders never seen before in the most familiar quarter of your life today.
verses.background: Krishna consents and exceeds the asking: behold My forms by the hundreds and thousands, all the gods and wonders never seen before, the whole universe standing as one in My body — but you cannot see Me with these eyes of yours; I give you the divine eye. Behold My sovereign yoga.
verses.hook: Which celestial beings does Arjuna find within Krishna's form?

views.text: 'Never seen before' means not seen by you or by anyone else in the human world.
All these are seen in His single form; the list is only illustrative — everything perceived in the world or described in scripture is there, plus marvels unseen in any world or text.
The universal form shows wonders of higher worlds never seen together, revealing the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Aśvins and Maruts as tiny fragments of God's body.

verses.devanagari:
इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम् ।
मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद् द्रष्टुमिच्छसि॥
verses.transliteration:
ihaikasthaṃ jagatkṛtsnaṃ paśyādya sacarācaram
mama dehe guḍākeśa yaccānyad draṣṭumicchasi
verses.essence: Behold today the entire universe, moving and unmoving, standing as one here in my body — and whatever else you wish to see.
verses.translation: Now behold, O Arjuna, in this, My body, the whole universe centred in one including the moving and the unmoving and whatever else thou desirest to see.

anvaya.parts: एक (one) + स्थ (standing): standing together in one
स (with) + चर (moving) + अचर (unmoving): together with all that moves and does not
गुडाका (sleep) + ईश (master): master of sleep

verses.explanation: The impossible offer: eka-stham, the whole of everything in one place — all space without losing its vastness, gathered into a single standing. And then the blank check: whatever else you wish to see. The vision will include even what Arjuna has not thought to ask about — including, terribly, the war's outcome.
verses.connection: Raises 11.6's pantheon to totality: not gods in a body, but the universe in one.
verses.reflection: Hold the thought a moment: the whole universe, standing in one body — and that body near you.
verses.background: Krishna consents and exceeds the asking: behold My forms by the hundreds and thousands, all the gods and wonders never seen before, the whole universe standing as one in My body — but you cannot see Me with these eyes of yours; I give you the divine eye. Behold My sovereign yoga.
verses.hook: Where exactly is Arjuna supposed to see the whole universe?

views.text: 'Whatever else you wish to see' includes victory and defeat — the very doubt Arjuna voiced in 2.6, 'whether we shall win or they shall conquer us'.
What could not be seen in millions of years of wandering is here at once, as limbs of His body; 'whatever else' also covers the causal ground of the world and the battle's outcome.
Everything, moving and still, past and future, exists within Krishna's body; Arjuna will even see the coming battle's outcome as part of the cosmic plan.

verses.devanagari:
न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा ।
दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम्॥
verses.transliteration:
na tu māṃ śakyase draṣṭumanenaiva svacakṣuṣā
divyaṃ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya me yogamaiśvaram
verses.essence: But you cannot see me with this eye of your own. I give you a divine eye: behold my sovereign yoga.
verses.translation: But thou art not able to behold Me with these thine own eyes; I give thee the divine eye; behold My lordly Yoga.

anvaya.form: verb, present, passive form, 2nd person singular ('you can')

anvaya.parts: स्व (own) + चक्षुस् (eye): one's own eye

verses.explanation: The technical clause of grace: the instrument must be replaced before the object can appear. Divyaṁ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ — the vision is not earned, climbed to, or unlocked; it is *given*, eye and all. Every genuine revelation has this structure: the seeing itself is part of the gift.
verses.connection: Answers 11.4's 'if I am able': you are not — so I will make you able.
verses.reflection: Admit which seeings are beyond your current eyes — and ask for the eye, not just the view.
verses.background: Krishna consents and exceeds the asking: behold My forms by the hundreds and thousands, all the gods and wonders never seen before, the whole universe standing as one in My body — but you cannot see Me with these eyes of yours; I give you the divine eye. Behold My sovereign yoga.
verses.hook: Why can't ordinary eyes see God's universal form?

views.text: 'My lordly yoga' is the superabundance of the power of yoga — the power of accomplishing the impossible.
The physical eye sees only limited, conditioned things; He is different in kind from everything and without limit, so a supernatural eye is needed.
The divine eye given is one made of knowledge, not of flesh; the yoga to be seen is His unique power to bring about what cannot otherwise happen.
God's divine form cannot be seen with material eyes, which is why people fail to recognise an Avatār. By grace he adds his own divine eyes, mind and intellect so the soul can see him.

verses.speaker: सञ्जय उवाच
verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरिः ।
दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम्॥
verses.transliteration:
evamuktvā tato rājanmahāyogeśvaro hariḥ
darśayāmāsa pārthāya paramaṃ rūpamaiśvaram
verses.essence: Sanjaya says: having spoken thus, O King, the great Lord of yoga, Hari, showed to Partha the supreme sovereign form.
verses.translation: Having thus spoken, O king, the great Lord of Yoga, hari (Krishna), showed to Arjuna His supreme form as the Lord.

anvaya.base: महत् · great; योग · yoga; ईश्वर · lord
anvaya.parts: महा (great) + योग (yoga) + ईश्वर (lord): the great lord of yoga

anvaya.base: हरि · remover, a name of Viṣṇu

anvaya.form: verb, periphrastic perfect, causative, 3rd person singular (he showed)

verses.explanation: The narrative frame returns — we are reminded that blind Dhritarashtra is hearing all this secondhand in a palace. Sanjaya, gifted his own divine sight by Vyasa, becomes our witness's witness: the most overwhelming vision in scripture reaches us through a chain of borrowed eyes.
verses.connection: Hands the telling to Sanjaya for the vision proper (11.9–14): what words can carry of it.
verses.reflection: Remember the chain of witnesses that carried this vision to you — and become a faithful link.
verses.background: Sanjaya takes over the telling, for Arjuna is past speech: the great Lord of yoga reveals the supreme form — countless mouths and eyes, divine ornaments and weapons, facing every direction, with the radiance of a thousand suns rising at once. Arjuna, hair standing on end, bows his head and joins his palms.
verses.hook: Who narrates the moment Krishna reveals his supreme form?

views.text: Sañjaya tells Dhṛtarāṣṭra that Hari, Nārāyaṇa, great and master of Yoga, then showed Arjuna his supreme divine form, the Cosmic form.
The one who shows the form is Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Brahman, now born as Arjuna's own cousin and sitting as his charioteer — the highest Lord close at hand.
Sanjaya, granted far vision by his guru Vyāsa, saw the cosmic form as Arjuna did, and calls Krishna the great Lord of yogis; the form's opulence inspires awe and reverence.

verses.devanagari:
अनेकवक्त्रनयनमनेकाद्भुतदर्शनम् ।
अनेकदिव्याभरणं दिव्यानेकोद्यतायुधम्॥
verses.transliteration:
anekavaktranayanamanekādbhutadarśanam
anekadivyābharaṇaṃ divyānekodyatāyudham
verses.essence: Of many mouths and eyes, of many wondrous sights, of many divine ornaments, with many divine weapons uplifted —
verses.translation: With numerous mouths and eyes, with numerous wonderful sights, with numerous divine ornaments, with numerous divine weapons uplifted (such a form He showed).

anvaya.base: अनेक · many; वक्त्र · mouth; नयन · eye
anvaya.form: compound adjective, neuter, accusative singular (describing the form)
anvaya.parts: अनेक (many) + वक्त्र (mouth) + नयन (eye): having many mouths and eyes
अनेक (many) + अद्भुत (wonderful) + दर्शन (sight): showing many wondrous sights
अनेक (many) + दिव्य (divine) + आभरण (ornament): wearing many divine ornaments
दिव्य (divine) + अनेक (many) + उद्यत (raised) + आयुध (weapon): bearing many raised divine weapons

verses.explanation: Language begins to fail in the only honest way: by repetition. Aneka, aneka, aneka — many, many, many — the word strikes four times because counting has already broken down. Mouths and eyes everywhere: nothing in this form has a back, a blind side, an away.
verses.connection: The first stroke of Sanjaya's description: multiplicity past numbering.
verses.reflection: Let one glimpse of the world's manyness today overwhelm your counting — and stand in the surplus.
verses.background: Sanjaya takes over the telling, for Arjuna is past speech: the great Lord of yoga reveals the supreme form — countless mouths and eyes, divine ornaments and weapons, facing every direction, with the radiance of a thousand suns rising at once. Arjuna, hair standing on end, bows his head and joins his palms.
verses.hook: What does the universal form look like at first sight?

views.text: The whole verse is a string of descriptions hanging on the verb 'He showed' in 11.9.
Arjuna saw the Lord everywhere and in everything; the whole manifestation appeared as one gigantic body, the Lord as the all-in-all.
All creation is the body of the cosmic form, so it holds countless faces, eyes and shapes; its marvels transcend space and time, beyond what the human intellect is used to grasping.

verses.devanagari:
दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनम् ।
सर्वाश्चर्यमयं देवमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम्॥
verses.transliteration:
divyamālyāmbaradharaṃ divyagandhānulepanam
sarvāścaryamayaṃ devamanantaṃ viśvatomukham
verses.essence: Wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine perfumes — all-wonderful, resplendent, boundless, with faces on every side.
verses.translation: Wearing divine garlands (necklaces) and apparel, anointed with divine unguents, the all-wonderful, resplendent (Being) endless with faces on all sides.

anvaya.base: माल्य · garland; अम्बर · garment; धर · wearing
anvaya.form: compound adjective, masculine, accusative singular (describing the God)

verses.explanation: Amid the overwhelming, tenderness: garlands, silks, sandal-fragrance — the universal form arrives *adorned*, beauty insisted upon even at the scale of everything. verses.connection: Completes the form's first portrait: terrifying scale, deliberately beautiful.
verses.reflection: Notice beauty insisting on itself even at terrifying scale — garlands on the infinite.

verses.explanation: The most famous simile in the poem, and the grammar keeps it humble: yadi... syāt — *if* a thousand suns rose at once, that *might* approach it. Śaṅkara adds 'or it might not'; Śrīdhara says there is no other comparison at all. A comparison that confesses failure inside its own construction. Millennia later, J. Robert Oppenheimer is reported to have recalled this verse as the first atomic fire rose at Trinity. Sanjaya, granted divine sight, still files his report as a failed comparison; that failure is the description.
verses.connection: Sanjaya's reach for a measure — and the admission that no measure holds.
verses.reflection: Recall the thousand-suns line at your next sunrise — one sun, and the comparison already fails.

views.text: Even a thousand suns 'might be — or might not be' like it; the point is that the Cosmic Person's brilliance surely surpasses even this.
The simile only illustrates that His splendour is infinite — by nature an inexhaustible radiance.
God's radiance is truly unlimited and cannot be measured by suns; Sanjaya uses a thousand suns, describing the unknown through the known, to say it had no parallel.

verses.reflection: Practice seeing one-in-many today: the family in its members, the forest in its trees, undivided.

views.text: Arjuna saw the whole universe, differentiated into groups of gods, manes, humans and others, united in the one Cosmic form, the body of Hari, God of gods.
With eyes given by grace, Arjuna saw matter and all selves at a single point in that body, with every class of being — exactly the universe chapter 10 described, now seen directly.
Every head was His head, every hand His hand; wherever Arjuna looked he saw only the Lord. Such a vision is beyond mind and senses and is realised in samādhi.
Arjuna saw all universes in a fraction of Krishna's body, the same cosmic form baby Krishna once showed his mother Yaśodā inside his mouth.

verses.explanation: The body answers before the mind can: hṛṣṭa-romā, every hair erect — awe registered in the skin. And the warrior's hands, trained for the bow, find their oldest gesture instead: kṛtāñjali, the añjali of palms joined. What follows (11.15–31) is not analysis but hymn — the only speech possible at this altitude.
verses.connection: The hinge from Sanjaya's report to Arjuna's own voice — description giving way to prayer.
verses.reflection: Let awe register in the body once today — gooseflesh, stilled breath — and bow instead of analyzing.

refs.note: Lists eight bodily signs of intense devotional love, such as trembling, tears and hair standing on end, which Arjuna shows here.

views.text: Filled with wonder, hair on end and full of humility, Arjuna bowed fully to the Lord in the Cosmic form and spoke with joined palms, voicing his own experience of what was revealed.
Overcome by seeing the One at a single point of whose being the whole universe rests, Arjuna bows down full length, like a stick, before speaking.
The great hero had reached true humility, shown by the bowed head and joined palms — the essential ingredient of devotion.
Awe stirred deep devotion in Arjuna; such love sometimes shows in the body, as with his hair standing on end, and he bowed with joined palms to speak.

verses.reflection: When the vision comes, in any size, do what Arjuna does: start naming what you see, gratefully.

The lotus seat is either Meru at the centre of the earth-lotus, or the lotus that grows from the Lord's own navel.
Arjuna sees beings from all three worlds within the form: the gods, Brahmā on his lotus, Shiva, the sages and the celestial serpents.

verses.explanation: Geometry surrenders: a form with no edge to start measuring from, no center to stand at, no boundary to finish at. The titles arrive fused: viśveśvara viśvarūpa — the Lord *of* all who is also the form *of* all.
verses.connection: The hymn's first vertigo: scale without coordinates.
verses.reflection: Stand before something with no findable edge today — sky, sea, love — and let geometry surrender.

Viśvarūpa means 'You who have the universe as Your body'; Viśveśvara, its controller. Because He is infinite, no end, middle or beginning can be seen.
What is limited by space and time has a start, middle and end; the Lord is not so limited, and is seen this way only with the eye His grace bestows.
Calling Krishna both the universe and its master, Arjuna finds no beginning, middle or end wherever he looks in the endless form.

verses.reflection: Respect the moments when looking is hard — some radiance is meant to overwhelm, not to be mastered.

views.text: Arjuna sees the Lord with diadem, mace and disc, a mass of brilliance hard to look at from every side, and immeasurable, meaning beyond limitation; from this power of Yoga he goes on to infer.
He is recognisable by His diadem, mace and discus, and yet remains indefinable and immeasurable.
He is hard to look at because His light is like blazing fire and sun; 'immeasurable' means no one can settle that He is just this.
Arjuna had worshipped the Lord with crown, club and discus, and the Lord showed him that same form now — He is in all forms and beyond all forms.
The form outshone thousands of suns, and Arjuna could look at it only with the divine eyes he had received; within it he also saw four-armed Vishnu with his emblems.

Sun-and-moon eyes beam grace on devotees and power against the hostile; the fire-mouth is the fire of time that consumes the world at dissolution.
'Without beginning, middle or end' means free of origin, continuance and dissolution.
Arjuna repeats himself out of sheer wonder. God has no beginning or end because space, time and causation exist within him; sun and moon draw their energy from him.

verses.explanation: Two words now travel together that the hymn cannot separate: adbhutam ugram — wondrous *and* terrible. And the audience widens: loka-trayaṁ pravyathitam, the three worlds themselves are shaking. This is no private vision; whatever Arjuna is seeing, all of reality is feeling.
verses.connection: The hymn turns: wonder begins its slide toward dread.
verses.reflection: When dread and wonder arrive together today, refuse to choose — adbhutam ugram, both are true.
verses.background: Arjuna finds words and they ascend from wonder to terror: all the gods in Your body, no beginning, middle, or end — then the blazing mouths, the worlds rushing in, the warriors of both armies streaming like rivers to the sea, like moths to flame, caught between the teeth. Trembling, he asks: who are You, of form so fierce, and what is Your purpose?
verses.hook: Why do the three worlds tremble before God's form?

refs.note: Says the world runs on the law of karma: whatever one does, one reaps the result, an example of the divine laws all must obey.

views.text: From here the Lord sets out to show the Pāṇḍavas' certain victory, to clear the doubt Arjuna voiced in 2.6.
Gods, asuras and other beings had gathered to watch the battle; they too were granted the divine eye, so Arjuna could see the Lord's sovereignty over friend, foe and neutral alike.
The worlds tremble not because they see the form but because all live under God's laws, like the law of karma; scientists discover such laws, but God alone makes them.

verses.devanagari:

verses.essence: These hosts of gods enter into you; some, terrified, praise you with joined palms. Crying 'Hail!', the throngs of great seers and siddhas praise you with abundant hymns.
verses.translation: Verily, into Thee enter these hosts of gods; some extol Thee in fear with joined palms; saying 'may it be well', bands of great sages and perfected ones praise Thee with hymns complete.

verses.explanation: The traffic of the vision is one-way: viśanti, the gods *enter* him — streams of divinity flowing back into their source. Even heaven's population divides by temperament: some, afraid, fold their palms and praise; the seers cry svasti — 'let there be well-being' — the word one says when well-being is suddenly in question.
verses.connection: The pantheon of 11.6 now seen in motion: not displayed in him but returning into him.
verses.reflection: Watch everything streaming back into its source — rivers, days, lives — and practice not clutching.
verses.background: Arjuna finds words and they ascend from wonder to terror: all the gods in Your body, no beginning, middle, or end — then the blazing mouths, the worlds rushing in, the warriors of both armies streaming like rivers to the sea, like moths to flame, caught between the teeth. Trembling, he asks: who are You, of form so fierce, and what is Your purpose?
verses.hook: What are the gods and sages doing within the universal form?

views.text: The gods entering Him are the warriors — gods such as the Vasus born as men to lighten the earth's burden; the seers cry 'svasti' on seeing portents of evil as battle nears.
The gods move toward Him in joy, seeing Him as the foundation of the universe; others, frightened by the terrible form, praise according to their understanding.
'Enter' means they take refuge in Him; the most terrified stand far off with joined hands, crying 'victory, victory, protect us'.
Arjuna sees Krishna as all-devouring time, consuming even the gods who enter with joined palms, while sages and perfected souls praise the Lord in thought, word and deed.

verses.translation: The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Visvedevas, the two Asvins, Maruts, the manes and the hosts of celestial singers, Yakshas, demons and the perfected ones, are all looking at Thee, in great amazement.

anvaya.base: वसु · a class of eight gods

anvaya.form: verb, present, 3rd person plural, middle voice

verses.explanation: The complete roll-call of the invisible world — gods, ancestors, celestial musicians, nature-spirits, even the asuras, heaven's opposition — and one verb for all of them: vīkṣante vismitāḥ, staring in astonishment. Whatever their rank or allegiance, before this form every being in the cosmos is reduced to the same expression.
verses.connection: Universalizes 11.21: nothing in existence is exempt from this audience.
verses.reflection: Remember that every order of being shares your astonishment — amazement is universal company.
verses.background: Arjuna finds words and they ascend from wonder to terror: all the gods in Your body, no beginning, middle, or end — then the blazing mouths, the worlds rushing in, the warriors of both armies streaming like rivers to the sea, like moths to flame, caught between the teeth. Trembling, he asks: who are You, of form so fierce, and what is Your purpose?
verses.hook: How do the heavenly beings react on seeing the cosmic form?

views.text: Names examples for each host: Hāhā and Hūhū among gandharvas, Kubera among yakṣas, Virocana among asuras, Kapila among siddhas — all alike staring in wonder.
Ūṣmapa means the ancestors, since scripture says the manes receive the hot portion of offerings.
All these beings owe their positions to God's power and serve under his laws, so they gaze at his cosmic form in wonder.

verses.devanagari:
रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रं
महाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम् ।
बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालं
दृष्ट्वा लोकाः प्रव्यथितास्तथाहम्॥
verses.transliteration:
rūpaṃ mahatte bahuvaktranetraṃ mahābāho bahubāhūrupādam
bahūdaraṃ bahudaṃṣṭrākarālaṃ dṛṣṭvā lokāḥ pravyathitāstathāham
verses.essence: Seeing your great form of many mouths and eyes, of many arms, thighs and feet, many bellies, terrible with many tusks — the worlds tremble, and so do I.
verses.translation: Having seen Thy immeasurable form with many mouths and eyes, O mighty-armed, with many arms, thighs and feet, with many stomachs and fearful with many teeth the worlds are terrified and so am I.

verses.explanation: A new detail enters the inventory and changes its tone: daṁṣṭrā, tusks — the form has fangs. And then the bravest small phrase in the hymn: tathā aham, *and so do I*. In chapter 1 the greatest archer alive spoke of grief and a reeling mind; now he names plain fear. The vision has found the bottom of his courage.
verses.connection: The dread becomes personal: from 'the worlds tremble' to 'I tremble.'
verses.reflection: When you finally tremble, say so plainly: and so do I. Honesty at the edge is also courage.
verses.background: Arjuna finds words and they ascend from wonder to terror: all the gods in Your body, no beginning, middle, or end — then the blazing mouths, the worlds rushing in, the warriors of both armies streaming like rivers to the sea, like moths to flame, caught between the teeth. Trembling, he asks: who are You, of form so fierce, and what is Your purpose?
verses.hook: Why does the sight of God's countless limbs terrify Arjuna?

refs.note: Describes the Supreme with thousands of heads, eyes and feet, enveloping the universe yet beyond it, as Arjuna now sees.
Says fire burns, the sun shines and even death runs out of fear of God, echoing the terror of the worlds.

views.text: Seeing the vast form with many mouths, eyes, arms, thighs, feet and bellies, fearful with many teeth, the creatures of the world are struck with terror, and so is Arjuna himself.
What makes the form so terrifying is above all its huge teeth; friendly, hostile and neutral beings alike are panic-stricken, and Arjuna with them.
Karāla means distorted, that is, wrathful (raudra): the form has turned fierce.
God's hands, feet and faces are everywhere; the terrified and the terrifying alike exist within his universal form.

verses.devanagari:
नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णं

दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्मा
धृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो॥
verses.transliteration:
nabhaḥspṛśaṃ dīptamanekavarṇaṃ vyāttānanaṃ dīptaviśālanetram
dṛṣṭvā hi tvāṃ pravyathitāntarātmā dhṛtiṃ na vindāmi śamaṃ ca viṣṇo
verses.essence: Touching the sky, blazing, many-colored, mouths agape, with vast flaming eyes — seeing you, my inmost self trembles, and I find neither steadiness nor calm, O Vishnu.
verses.translation: On seeing Thee (the Cosmic Form) touching the sky, shining in many colours, with mouths wide open, with large fiery eyes, I am terrified at heart and find neither courage nor peace, O Vishnu.

anvaya.form: compound adjective, masculine, accusative singular (describing you)
anvaya.parts: नभस् (sky) + स्पृश् (touching): reaching up to the sky
अनेक (many) + वर्ण (colour): of many colours
व्यात्त (wide open) + आनन (mouth): whose mouths gape open

anvaya.base: दीप्त · blazing; विशाल · huge; नेत्र · eye
anvaya.parts: दीप्त (blazing) + विशाल (large) + नेत्र (eye): with large fiery eyes

anvaya.form: compound adjective, masculine, nominative singular (describing I)
anvaya.parts: प्रव्यथित (deeply shaken) + अन्तरात्मन् (inner self, mind): one whose inner self is shaken

verses.explanation: Vyāttānanam — mouths *opened wide*: the fire-mouths of 11.19 are no longer emblematic; they are gaping. Arjuna's report is clinical in its honesty: dhṛti and śama, steadiness and calm, qualities the earlier chapters kept urging on him — na vindāmi, I cannot find them. The curriculum has met something its exercises did not cover.
verses.connection: The vision overruns the very equanimity chapters 2–6 had built.
verses.reflection: When your trained steadiness fails before something vast, let it fail honestly — then pray.
verses.background: Arjuna finds words and they ascend from wonder to terror: all the gods in Your body, no beginning, middle, or end — then the blazing mouths, the worlds rushing in, the warriors of both armies streaming like rivers to the sea, like moths to flame, caught between the teeth. Trembling, he asks: who are You, of form so fierce, and what is Your purpose?
verses.hook: Why does Arjuna lose his peace and courage before this form?

views.text: 'Many-coloured' is glossed as having many frightening forms. Seeing him touch heaven, blazing and open-mouthed, with fiery eyes, Arjuna is terrified in mind and finds neither steadiness nor calm.

'Touching the sky' means reaching the Supreme Heaven beyond matter; dhṛti is the steadiness that holds up the body, śama the peace of mind and senses. 'Viṣṇu' means the Pervader, seen filling everything.
'Touching the sky' simply means filling the space between heaven and earth; Arjuna finds neither courage nor calm.

The vision of majesty turned Arjuna's intimate friendship into awe and fear. Love forgets God's greatness to relate closely, as Braj's cowherd boys did, and reverence for power can crowd that intimacy out.

verses.devanagari:
दंष्ट्राकरालानि च ते मुखानि
दृष्ट्वैव कालानलसन्निभानि ।
दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्म
प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास॥
verses.transliteration:
daṃṣṭrākarālāni ca te mukhāni dṛṣṭvaiva kālānalasannibhāni
diśo na jāne na labhe ca śarma prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa
verses.essence: Seeing your mouths, terrible with tusks, like the fires of time's ending — I lose the directions and find no peace. Be gracious, Lord of gods, dwelling of the universe!
verses.translation: Having seen Thy mouths fearful with teeth (blazing) like the fires of cosmic dissolution, I know not the four quarters, nor do I find peace. Have mercy, O Lord of the gods, O abode of the universe.

anvaya.form: adjective, neuter, accusative plural (describing the mouths)
anvaya.parts: दंष्ट्रा (tusk, fang) + कराल (dreadful): made dreadful by tusks

anvaya.form: adjective, neuter, accusative plural (describing the mouths)
anvaya.parts: काल (time, doom) + अनल (fire) + सन्निभ (resembling): like the fire that ends the worlds

anvaya.base: दिश् · direction, quarter of the sky

anvaya.parts: देव (god) + ईश (lord): the lord of the gods
जगत् (world) + निवास (dwelling): one in whom the world dwells

verses.explanation: The simile names what the mouths are: kālānala, the fire of Time at the world's end. Diśo na jāne — the warrior who navigates battlefields by the directions has lost them; there is no 'away' from a form that faces everywhere. And so the hymn breaks into its first cry: prasīda — mercy. Praise has run out; petition begins.
verses.connection: The turning word of the chapter: from describing the vision to begging relief from it.
verses.reflection: In your most lost hour, use Arjuna's words: I know not the directions — be gracious.
verses.background: Arjuna finds words and they ascend from wonder to terror: all the gods in Your body, no beginning, middle, or end — then the blazing mouths, the worlds rushing in, the warriors of both armies streaming like rivers to the sea, like moths to flame, caught between the teeth. Trembling, he asks: who are You, of form so fierce, and what is Your purpose?
verses.hook: Why does Arjuna beg for mercy before Krishna's fiery mouths?

views.text: Merely seeing the mouths, terrible with teeth and like the fire of Dissolution, Arjuna loses all sense of direction and finds no comfort, so he asks the Lord of gods, Abode of the Universe, to be gracious.
Takes prasīda as a plea to be restored: act so that I may return to my natural condition. Deveśa is widened to mean overlord even of gods like Brahmā.
Traces the loss of direction to fear: Arjuna no longer knows east from west because terror has seized him, and so he finds no ease.
Glosses Jagannivāsa as the substratum of the universe and kālānala as the fire that consumes the worlds at dissolution, Time being the consumer of all that is manifest.
The universal form is not different from Krishna, yet seeing it dries up Arjuna's friendly ease; frightened, he thinks Krishna is angry and pleads for mercy.

verses.devanagari:
अमी च त्वां धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राः
सर्वे सहैवावनिपालसङ्घैः ।
भीष्मो द्रोणः सूतपुत्रस्तथासौ
सहास्मदीयैरपि योधमुख्यैः॥
verses.transliteration:
amī ca tvāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ sarve sahaivāvanipālasaṅghaiḥ
bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sūtaputrastathāsau sahāsmadīyairapi yodhamukhyaiḥ
verses.essence: And all these sons of Dhritarashtra, together with the hosts of kings — Bhishma, Drona, and that son of a charioteer too, along with our own chief warriors —
verses.translation: All the sons of Dhritarashtra, with the hosts of kings of the earth, Bhishma, Drona and Karna, with the chief among our warriors.

anvaya.form: pronoun, 2nd person, accusative singular (goal of 'enter' in 11.27)

anvaya.base: अवनिपालसङ्घ · multitude of rulers of the earth
anvaya.parts: अवनि (earth) + पाल (protector) + सङ्घ (host): hosts of earth-protectors, i.e. kings
सूत (charioteer) + पुत्र (son): the charioteer's son, Karna
योध (warrior) + मुख्य (chief): the chief among warriors

verses.explanation: The vision pivots from cosmos to Kurukshetra: suddenly, inside the universal form, Arjuna recognizes *faces* — the very men arrayed outside it. Bhishma, Drona, Karna... and the sentence's most terrible word is its quietest: asmadīyaiḥ, *ours too*. Both armies. The vision is not taking sides.
verses.connection: The war enters the vision — chapter 1's named beloveds reappearing inside the fire.
verses.reflection: Look once today at both sides of your conflict inside one frame — the vision takes no sides.
verses.background: Arjuna finds words and they ascend from wonder to terror: all the gods in Your body, no beginning, middle, or end — then the blazing mouths, the worlds rushing in, the warriors of both armies streaming like rivers to the sea, like moths to flame, caught between the teeth. Trembling, he asks: who are You, of form so fierce, and what is Your purpose?
verses.hook: Which great warriors does Arjuna see rushing toward Krishna?

refs.note: Bhīṣma, dying on his bed of arrows, prays to Krishna who cut short the opposing generals' lives by a glance, showing Bhīṣma knew opposing the Lord meant death.

views.text: Notes that 'into you' (tvām) hangs on 'rapidly enter' in the next verse, and names 'our warriors' as Dhṛṣṭadyumna and the other Pāṇḍava leaders.
Sees this as the Lord's earlier invitation to 'see whatever else you wish' being fulfilled: Arjuna now watches the coming victory and defeat of this battle inside the cosmic body.
God is beyond time, so Arjuna sees the coming future: Bhīṣma, Droṇa and Karṇa, heroic yet on the side of wrong, are destined to die in this war.

verses.devanagari:

केचिद्विलग्ना दशनान्तरेषु

vaktrāṇi te tvaramāṇā viśanti daṃṣṭrākarālāni bhayānakāni
kecidvilagnā daśanāntareṣu sandṛśyante cūrṇitairuttamāṅgaiḥ

verses.translation: Some hurriedly enter Thy mouths with their terrible teeth, fearful to behold. Some are found sticking in the gaps between the teeth with their heads crushed to powder.

adjective, neuter, accusative plural (describing the mouths)
anvaya.parts: दंष्ट्रा (tusk, fang) + कराल (dreadful): made dreadful by tusks

anvaya.form: adjective, neuter, accusative plural (describing the mouths)

anvaya.parts: दशन (tooth) + अन्तर (gap): the gaps between teeth

anvaya.form: verb, present passive, 3rd person plural (are seen)

anvaya.base: चूर्णय · to grind to powder (from चूर्ण, powder)

verses.explanation: Tvaramāṇāḥ — *hurrying*: the warriors are not dragged; they rush, as if eager, as if the rushing were their own idea. This is the vision's most pitiless disclosure: what looks from the field like strategy and valor looks from here like moths' haste. And some hang caught in the teeth — the detail no theology fully domesticates.
verses.connection: Completes 11.26: the future of the war shown as already in progress.
verses.reflection: Watch the hurry in yourself and others toward what consumes — and step out of one such rushing today.
verses.background: Arjuna finds words and they ascend from wonder to terror: all the gods in Your body, no beginning, middle, or end — then the blazing mouths, the worlds rushing in, the warriors of both armies streaming like rivers to the sea, like moths to flame, caught between the teeth. Trembling, he asks: who are You, of form so fierce, and what is Your purpose?
verses.hook: What becomes of the warriors who enter Krishna's mouths?

views.text: Pictures those caught between the teeth as sticking there like eaten meat, heads crushed, among the many who have already entered.
Glosses tvaramāṇāḥ as 'running, as it were': the warriors seem to race toward the fanged mouths of their own accord.
God's teeth are his power of destruction, which with time grinds everyone down; Arjuna watches generals of both armies being crushed, seeing the imminent future within God.

verses.devanagari:

समुद्रमेवाभिमुखा द्रवन्ति ।
तथा तवामी नरलोकवीरा
विशन्ति वक्त्राण्यभिविज्वलन्ति॥

yathā nadīnāṃ bahavo'mbuvegāḥ samudramevābhimukhā dravanti
tathā tavāmī naralokavīrā viśanti vaktrāṇyabhivijvalanti
verses.essence: As the many torrents of rivers race toward the ocean alone, so do these heroes of the human world enter your flaming mouths.
verses.translation: Verily, just as many torrents of rivers flow towards the ocean, even so these heroes in the world of men enter Thy flaming mouths.

anvaya.parts: अम्बु (water) + वेग (rush, force): rushing currents of water

anvaya.base: नरलोकवीर · hero of the world of men
anvaya.parts: नर (man) + लोक (world) + वीर (hero): heroes of the world of men

anvaya.form: present participle, neuter accusative plural (describing the mouths)

verses.explanation: The first of two similes, and the gentler one to look at: rivers to the sea. Their torrents run samudram eva — toward the ocean alone — down a thousand separate channels, and none can turn back. So the heroes of the human world enter the blazing mouths, each by his own road, all to one end. Śrīdhara reads this as entry without choice, carried by a current; the moths of the next verse will show the other kind.
verses.connection: First reading of the rushing: inevitability as return.
verses.reflection: Try the river-reading on a loss today: not destruction, but a long-planned return to the sea.
verses.background: Arjuna finds words and they ascend from wonder to terror: all the gods in Your body, no beginning, middle, or end — then the blazing mouths, the worlds rushing in, the warriors of both armies streaming like rivers to the sea, like moths to flame, caught between the teeth.
